# Step 10: Duplicates and repeated records

```{r}
#| label: duplicate-checks

dictionary_variables <- dictionary$variable_name

values_per_record <- rowSums(as.data.frame(lapply(working_data[dictionary_variables], is_filled)))
empty_record <- values_per_record == 0
record_issues("duplicates", which(empty_record), "(whole record)", NA, "record has no values",
              "error", "record removed")

# Removals before duplicate screening, counted once each in this order:
# coordinates, study region, measurements.
missing_position <- is.na(latitude) | is.na(longitude)
measurement_present <- sapply(stem_measurement_variables, function(variable) is_filled(working_data[[variable]]))
measurement_present <- matrix(measurement_present, nrow = number_of_records)  # Keeps a table even for one record.
lacks_stem_measurement <- rowSums(measurement_present) == 0

removed_no_position <- !empty_record & require_coordinates_in_public_file & missing_position
removed_imprecise   <- !empty_record & !removed_no_position & remove_imprecise_positions & imprecise
removed_coordinates <- removed_no_position | removed_imprecise
removed_outside     <- !empty_record & !removed_coordinates & outside_study_region
removed_implausible <- !empty_record & !removed_coordinates & !removed_outside & implausible_measurement
no_stem_measurement <- !empty_record & !removed_coordinates & !removed_outside & !removed_implausible &
  lacks_stem_measurement
removed_measurement <- removed_implausible | no_stem_measurement
record_issues("public file", which(removed_no_position), pair_name, NA, "latitude or longitude missing",
              "error", "record removed")
record_issues("public file", which(no_stem_measurement), paste(stem_measurement_variables, collapse = ", "),
              NA, "no stem measurement recorded", "error", "record removed")

# Duplicates are screened only among records that passed those checks, so the
# copy kept is never one removed for another reason.
passed_checks <- !empty_record & !removed_coordinates & !removed_outside & !removed_measurement
record_text <- do.call(paste, c(lapply(working_data[dictionary_variables],
                                       function(values) coalesce(values, "\u0001")),
                                sep = "\u0002"))
record_text[!passed_checks] <- NA
first_copy       <- match(record_text, record_text)
duplicate_record <- passed_checks & first_copy != seq_len(number_of_records)
record_issues("duplicates", which(duplicate_record), "(whole record)",
              paste("same as record", first_copy[duplicate_record]),
              "exact duplicate of an earlier record", "error", "record removed")
kept_so_far <- passed_checks & !duplicate_record

# Repeated records are reduced to one: the record with the most values is
# kept (the earlier one if equally complete), and the others are removed.
candidates <- working_data %>%
  mutate(record_number = row_number(), values = values_per_record,
         tree = .data[[tree_identity_variable]], date = .data[[date_variable]],
         position = paste(.data[[latitude_variable]], .data[[longitude_variable]]))

# The same tree recorded more than once on one date.
repeated_visit <- candidates %>%
  filter(kept_so_far, is_filled(tree), is_filled(date)) %>%
  group_by(source_file, tree, date) %>%
  filter(n() > 1) %>%
  arrange(desc(values), record_number, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(kept_record = first(record_number)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(record_number != kept_record)
record_issues("duplicates", repeated_visit$record_number, tree_identity_variable, repeated_visit$tree,
              paste("same tree recorded again on the same date; record", repeated_visit$kept_record, "kept"),
              "error", "record removed")
repeated_record <- seq_len(number_of_records) %in% repeated_visit$record_number
kept_so_far <- kept_so_far & !repeated_record

# Different trees at one position in one file, such as a copied plot centre:
# the tree with the most complete record is kept with all its records.
shared_position <- candidates %>%
  filter(kept_so_far, !is.na(.data[[latitude_variable]]), is_filled(tree)) %>%
  group_by(source_file, position) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(tree) > 1) %>%
  arrange(desc(values), record_number, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(kept_tree = first(tree), kept_record = first(record_number)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(tree != kept_tree)
record_issues("duplicates", shared_position$record_number, pair_name, shared_position$position,
              paste("same position as a different tree in the same file; record",
                    shared_position$kept_record, "kept"), "error", "record removed")
repeated_record <- repeated_record | seq_len(number_of_records) %in% shared_position$record_number
kept_so_far <- kept_so_far & !repeated_record

# The same observation in two or more files: same position (to 5 decimal
# places, about 1 m), same full date and same tree type. Records on different
# dates are kept as repeat visits.
cross_file_repeat <- candidates %>%
  mutate(day = str_sub(date, 1, 10), type = coalesce(.data[[tree_type_variable]], "")) %>%
  filter(kept_so_far, !is.na(.data[[latitude_variable]]), str_detect(coalesce(day, ""), "^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$")) %>%
  group_by(position, day, type) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(source_file) > 1) %>%
  arrange(desc(values), record_number, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(kept_file = first(source_file), kept_record = first(record_number)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(source_file != kept_file)
record_issues("duplicates", cross_file_repeat$record_number, pair_name,
              paste(cross_file_repeat$position, cross_file_repeat$day),
              paste("same position and date as record", cross_file_repeat$kept_record,
                    "in", cross_file_repeat$kept_file, "(kept)"), "error", "record removed")
repeated_record <- repeated_record | seq_len(number_of_records) %in% cross_file_repeat$record_number
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
show_step_results("duplicates", "Duplicate checks.")
```

# Step 11: Overlap with the TRY Plant Trait Database

```{r}
#| label: try-overlap

# Results of TRY_comparison_check.R.
try_summary_file <- if (exists("try_results_folder")) file.path(try_results_folder, "try_cross_check_summary.csv") else ""
try_summary <- if (is_filled(try_summary_file) && file.exists(try_summary_file)) read_as_text(try_summary_file) else NULL
try_value <- function(measure) {
  value <- try_summary$value[try_summary$measure == measure]
  if (length(value) == 0) NA_character_ else value[1]
}
try_species <- "Adansonia digitata"
try_text <- if (is.null(try_summary)) {
  "The TRY cross-check has not been run; run TRY_comparison_check.R before this document."
} else {
  georeferenced <- as_number(try_value(paste(try_species, "observations with coordinates")))
  near          <- as_number(try_value(paste(try_species, "observations within 50 m of a BAM baobab")))
  probable      <- as_number(try_value(paste(try_species, "probable duplicates of BAM records")))
  paste0("A TRY observation was classified as a probable duplicate if it lay within 50 m of a baobab in the ",
         "harmonised dataset and matched it in height or contributor name. TRY held ",
         try_value(paste(try_species, "observations in TRY")), " *", try_species, "* observations across ",
         try_value(paste(try_species, "traits in TRY")), " traits (", try_value(paste(try_species, "trait names in TRY")),
         "), of which ", georeferenced, " were georeferenced. ",
         if (!is.na(near) && near == 0) paste0("None of the georeferenced observations lay within 50 m of a baobab ",
                                               "record, so no probable duplicates were found.") else
           paste0(near, " georeferenced observations lay within 50 m of a baobab record, and ", probable,
                  " were classified as probable duplicates (see try_bam_duplicate_check.csv)."))
}
```

`r try_text`

# Step 12: Observation comments

Typing errors in the observers' comments are corrected with the list in `comment_corrections.csv` (input tables folder), which gives each error as recorded and its correction (for example, "Wholes" to "Holes" and "Gauging" to "Gouging"). A correction is applied only where the listed text stands as a whole word, in any letter case, and a capital first letter is kept. Every comment changed is logged with its original and corrected text in `qaqc_corrections_applied.csv`. `r if (check_comment_spelling) paste0("The corrected comments are then checked with the hunspell spelling checker (", spelling_dictionary, " dictionary). Words it does not recognise are listed with suggested corrections in comment_spelling_review.csv; they are not changed. A word confirmed as an error is corrected by adding it to comment_corrections.csv. The checker cannot find a real word used in error, such as \"wholes\" for \"holes\", so these are found by reading the comments.") else ""`

```{r}
#| label: comment-corrections

comment_corrections <- read_correction_table(input_paths$comment_corrections_file,
                                             "text_as_recorded", "corrected_text")
if (!file.exists(input_paths$comment_corrections_file)) {
  print_to_console("comment_corrections.csv was not found in ", input_tables_folder,
                   "; comments are not corrected.")
}

# Each listed correction is applied to every comment variable in turn, and the
# number of comments it changed is counted.
comment_correction_counts <- comment_corrections %>%
  select(text_as_recorded, corrected_text) %>%
  mutate(comments_corrected = 0L)
for (variable in comment_variables) {
  comments_before <- working_data[[variable]]
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(comment_corrections))) {
    values  <- working_data[[variable]]
    updated <- correct_comment_text(values, comment_corrections$text_as_recorded[i],
                                    comment_corrections$corrected_text[i])
    comment_correction_counts$comments_corrected[i] <- comment_correction_counts$comments_corrected[i] +
      sum(coalesce(updated != values, FALSE))
    working_data[[variable]] <- updated
  }
  comment_changed <- coalesce(comments_before != working_data[[variable]], FALSE)
  record_issues("comments", which(comment_changed), variable, comments_before[comment_changed],
                "typing error listed in comment_corrections.csv", "note", "text corrected")
  record_corrections("comments", which(comment_changed), variable, comments_before[comment_changed],
                     working_data[[variable]][comment_changed], "comment_corrections.csv")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: comment-spelling

# Words not recognised by hunspell are listed for review. Words in the
# accepted list, species names, country names and words containing digits or
# written in capitals (abbreviations) are not listed.
comment_spelling_review <- tibble(word = character(), occurrences = integer(), records = integer(),
                                  suggestions = character(), example_comment = character())
spelling_checked <- FALSE
if (check_comment_spelling && length(comment_variables) > 0) {
  if (!requireNamespace("hunspell", quietly = TRUE)) {
    print_to_console("The hunspell package is not installed; the spelling check of comments is skipped. ",
                     "Install it with install.packages(\"hunspell\").")
  } else {
    spelling_checked <- TRUE
    comment_text <- tibble(record_number = rep(seq_len(number_of_records), length(comment_variables)),
                           comment = unlist(working_data[comment_variables], use.names = FALSE)) %>%
      filter(is_filled(comment))
    known_words <- unique(c(words_accepted_in_comments,
                            unlist(str_split(na.omit(working_data[[species_variable]]), "\\s+")),
                            unlist(str_split(na.omit(working_data$country), "\\s+"))))
    unrecognised <- hunspell::hunspell(comment_text$comment, ignore = known_words,
                                       dict = hunspell::dictionary(spelling_dictionary))
    flagged_words <- tibble(record_number = rep(comment_text$record_number, lengths(unrecognised)),
                            comment = rep(comment_text$comment, lengths(unrecognised)),
                            word = unlist(unrecognised)) %>%
      filter(!str_detect(word, "\\d"), word != str_to_upper(word), nchar(word) > 2)
    if (nrow(flagged_words) > 0) {
      comment_spelling_review <- flagged_words %>%
        group_by(word) %>%
        summarise(occurrences = n(), records = n_distinct(record_number),
                  example_comment = str_trunc(first(comment), 100), .groups = "drop") %>%
        arrange(desc(occurrences), word)
      comment_spelling_review$suggestions <- vapply(
        hunspell::hunspell_suggest(comment_spelling_review$word, dict = hunspell::dictionary(spelling_dictionary)),
        function(found) paste(head(found, 3), collapse = ", "), character(1))
      comment_spelling_review <- relocate(comment_spelling_review, suggestions, .after = records)
      record_issues("comments", unique(flagged_words$record_number), paste(comment_variables, collapse = ", "),
                    NA, "word not recognised by the spelling checker", "note", "kept; listed for review")
    }
    print_to_console("\nSpelling check of comments: ", nrow(comment_spelling_review),
                     " words not recognised; see comment_spelling_review.csv")
  }
}
```

# Public data file

The public file, `r input_paths$public_file_name`, is saved in its own folder (`public_data`). It contains the dictionary variables in dictionary order, except those withheld (`r paste(dictionary$variable_name[dictionary$withheld & dictionary$kind != "email"], collapse = ", ")` and the email address), followed by the published derived variables in @tbl-derived`r if (publish_source_columns) " and the source columns" else ""`. `r if (!publish_source_columns) "The source columns, which record the file, sheet and row of each record, are not published; they remain in the internal reports." else ""` Email addresses are removed: the email variable is withheld, and any email address written inside another value (for example, a comment) is replaced by "\[email address removed\]". Observer names are published only as names from the contributor list (Step 2) and only where the observer answered "yes" to the visibility question; where the answer is "no", observer_name shows "`r anonymous_label`" (Step 3). The identity of sensitive species is withheld (Step 9). Only records `r if (include_african_islands) "in Africa" else "on mainland Africa"` are included (Step 5). Where the same tree was recorded more than once on one date, different trees share one position in one file, or records in different files share position, date and tree type, only the most complete record is kept (Step 10); duplicates are screened only among records that passed the coordinate, study-region and measurement checks, so the copy kept is never one removed for another reason. Each record carries its data collection method (`data_collection_method`), the name of the raw-input folder that holds its source file. A record is removed if its latitude or longitude is missing, or if all of `r paste(stem_measurement_variables, collapse = ", ")` are blank (a record with at least one stem measurement is kept). Observation dates are written as ISO 8601 dates without a time: `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `YYYY-MM` and `YYYY` where the day or month was not recorded. Every empty value is written as NA.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-derived
#| tbl-cap: "Variables derived during quality control. Only those marked yes are written to the public file."
knitr::kable(rename(derived_variables, Variable = variable_name, Published = in_public,
                    Description = description),
             format = "pipe")
```

```{r}
#| label: build-public-file

# Records kept: those that passed every check and were not removed as
# duplicates (Step 10).
keep_record <- passed_checks & !duplicate_record & !repeated_record

if (!is.na(observer_name_variable)) working_data[[observer_name_variable]][names_withheld] <- anonymous_label

# Identifiers come from the source file, sheet, row and column group, so they
# persist across releases.
identity_columns <- intersect(c("source_file", "source_sheet", "source_row", "source_column_group"), names(working_data))
source_key <- do.call(paste, c(lapply(working_data[identity_columns], coalesce, ""), sep = "|"))
source_hash <- unname(vapply(source_key, digest::digest, character(1), algo = "md5", serialize = FALSE))
working_data$record_id <- paste0(record_id_prefix, "-", toupper(substr(source_hash, 1, 10)))
if (anyDuplicated(working_data$record_id[keep_record]) > 0) {
  stop("Two records received the same record identifier.", call. = FALSE)
}

# Photographs are copied under names derived from the record identifier;
# sub-folders are searched too.

# photo_name_key() reduces a photograph reference or path to a lower-case file
# name without extension.
photo_name_key <- function(references) {
  cleaned <- vapply(coalesce(references, ""), function(text) {
    tryCatch(utils::URLdecode(text), error = function(e) text)
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  cleaned <- str_replace_all(cleaned, "\\\\", "/")
  file_names <- str_extract_all(cleaned, "[^/?=&#]+\\.[A-Za-z0-9]{2,5}(?=$|[?&#])")
  last_name  <- vapply(file_names, function(found) if (length(found)) found[length(found)] else NA_character_,
                       character(1))
  last_name  <- coalesce(last_name, basename(cleaned))
  tolower(tools::file_path_sans_ext(last_name))
}

photo_lookup <- tibble()
if (is_filled(input_paths$photo_source_folder)) {
  photo_folder_out <- file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "photographs_for_public")
  dir.create(photo_folder_out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  photo_files <- list.files(input_paths$photo_source_folder,
                            pattern = "\\.(jpe?g|png|gif|bmp|tiff?|heic|webp)$",
                            ignore.case = TRUE, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
  message("Photographs found in ", input_paths$photo_source_folder, " and its sub-folders: ",
          length(photo_files))
  photo_key <- photo_name_key(photo_files)

  # File names found in several sub-folders cannot be matched safely and are
  # not copied.
  repeated_keys <- unique(photo_key[duplicated(photo_key)])

  for (photo_number in seq_along(photograph_variables)) {
    variable  <- photograph_variables[photo_number]
    reference <- working_data[[variable]]
    reference_key <- photo_name_key(reference)
    file_index <- match(reference_key, photo_key)

    ambiguous <- keep_record & is_filled(reference) & reference_key %in% repeated_keys
    record_issues("photographs", which(ambiguous), variable, reference[ambiguous],
                  "photograph file name found in more than one sub-folder", "warning",
                  "photograph not copied; rename the files so that each name is unique")

    not_found <- keep_record & is_filled(reference) & is.na(file_index)
    record_issues("photographs", which(not_found), variable, reference[not_found],
                  "photograph file not found in the photo folder", "warning", "reference kept")

    found <- keep_record & !is.na(file_index) & !ambiguous
    new_names <- paste0(working_data$record_id[found], "_", photo_number, ".",
                        tolower(tools::file_ext(photo_files[file_index[found]])))
    file.copy(photo_files[file_index[found]], file.path(photo_folder_out, new_names), overwrite = TRUE)
    photo_lookup <- bind_rows(photo_lookup, tibble(record_id = working_data$record_id[found],
                                                   variable_name = variable,
                                                   original_reference = reference[found],
                                                   public_file_name = new_names))
    working_data[[variable]][found] <- new_names
  }
}

record_flags <- current_issues() %>%
  filter(!is.na(record_number), severity %in% c("error", "warning"),
         !action_taken %in% c("record removed")) %>%
  distinct(record_number, flag = paste0(check, " (", variable_name, ")")) %>%
  group_by(record_number) %>%
  summarise(qaqc_flags = paste(flag, collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop")
working_data$qaqc_flags <- record_flags$qaqc_flags[match(seq_len(number_of_records),
                                                         record_flags$record_number)]

# All kept records with every column, for the internal reports only.
kept_records <- working_data[keep_record, ]

public_variables <- dictionary$variable_name[!dictionary$withheld]
public_columns <- c("record_id", public_variables,
                    setdiff(published_derived_variables, "record_id"),
                    if (publish_source_columns) source_columns)
public_dataset <- working_data[keep_record, public_columns]
public_record_numbers <- which(keep_record)

# Observation dates are published without a time; partial dates keep only the
# parts recorded (YYYY-MM or YYYY).
public_dataset[[date_variable]] <- str_sub(public_dataset[[date_variable]], 1, 10)

columns_not_published <- c(dictionary$variable_name[dictionary$withheld],
                           setdiff(derived_variables$variable_name, published_derived_variables),
                           if (!publish_source_columns) source_columns)

# E-mail addresses written inside any value are removed.
for (column in public_columns) {
  values <- public_dataset[[column]]
  contains_email <- is_filled(values) & str_detect(values, email_address_pattern)
  record_issues("public file", public_record_numbers[contains_email], column, NA,
                "email address found in text", "note", "email address replaced")
  public_dataset[[column]][contains_email] <-
    str_replace_all(values[contains_email], email_address_pattern, "[email address removed]")
}
for (variable in dictionary$variable_name[dictionary$withheld]) {
  record_issues("public file", NA, variable, NA, "personal data", "note", "variable withheld")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: final-verification

# Final checks
# No withheld column is present.
confirm(!any(columns_not_published %in% names(public_dataset)),
        paste("a withheld column is still present:",
              paste(intersect(columns_not_published, names(public_dataset)), collapse = ", ")))
confirm(!any(str_starts(names(public_dataset), fixed(source_column_prefix))) || publish_source_columns,
        "a source column is still present.")
# No e-mail address appears anywhere.
confirm(!any(map_lgl(public_dataset, ~ any(str_detect(.x, email_address_pattern), na.rm = TRUE))),
        "an email address is still present.")
confirm(all(follows_dictionary_style(names(public_dataset))),
        "a column name does not follow the dictionary format.")
confirm(identical(intersect(names(public_dataset), dictionary$variable_name), public_variables),
        "the dictionary variables are not in dictionary order.")
coordinate_format <- paste0("^-?\\d{1,3}\\.\\d{", coordinate_decimal_places, "}$")
confirm(all(str_detect(na.omit(c(public_dataset[[latitude_variable]], public_dataset[[longitude_variable]])),
                       coordinate_format)),
        "a coordinate does not have the required number of decimal places.")
confirm(all(is.na(public_dataset[[latitude_variable]]) == is.na(public_dataset[[longitude_variable]])),
        "a record has only one coordinate.")
if (require_coordinates_in_public_file) {
  confirm(!any(is.na(public_dataset[[latitude_variable]]) | is.na(public_dataset[[longitude_variable]])),
          "a record has a missing latitude or longitude.")
}
public_measurement_count <- rowSums(as.data.frame(lapply(public_dataset[stem_measurement_variables], is_filled)))
confirm(all(public_measurement_count > 0),
        "a record has no stem measurement.")
confirm(!any(outside_study_region[public_record_numbers]),
        "a record lies outside the study region.")
confirm(all(is_filled(public_dataset$record_id)) && anyDuplicated(public_dataset$record_id) == 0,
        "record identifiers are missing or repeated.")
confirm(all(str_detect(na.omit(public_dataset[[date_variable]]), "^\\d{4}(-\\d{2}(-\\d{2})?)?$")),
        "an observation date is not an ISO 8601 date without a time.")
confirm(!species_variable %in% names(public_dataset) || !"species" %in% withheld_from_public_file,
        "the species as recorded is still in the public file.")
# Rounded values have no more decimal places than set.
for (role_name in names(decimal_places_by_role)) {
  variable <- variable_for(role_name)
  if (is.na(variable) || !variable %in% names(public_dataset)) next
  confirm(all(count_decimal_places(na.omit(public_dataset[[variable]])) <= decimal_places_by_role[[role_name]]),
          paste(variable, "has more decimal places than set in decimal_places_by_role."))
}
# Every observer who declined is shown as "Anonymous".
if (!is.na(observer_name_variable) && !is.na(public_access_variable)) {
  if (withhold_names_answered_no) {
    answered_no <- str_to_lower(working_data[[public_access_variable]][public_record_numbers]) %in% "no"
    confirm(all(public_dataset[[observer_name_variable]][answered_no] %in% anonymous_label),
            "a name is published although the observer answered no.")
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: save-outputs

# The full issue log is for internal use only, as it holds original values.
record_identifiers <- tibble(record_number = seq_len(number_of_records),
                             record_id = working_data$record_id) %>%
  bind_cols(harmonised_data[intersect(c(tree_identity_variable, source_columns), names(harmonised_data))])
qaqc_issues <- current_issues() %>%
  left_join(record_identifiers, by = "record_number") %>%
  relocate(step, record_number, record_id) %>%
  arrange(factor(severity, levels = c("error", "warning", "note")), step, record_number)

# Each variable is described from, in order: the dictionary's
# variable_description column, the standard description of its role, the
# dictionary label, or the description of a derived variable.
dictionary_row <- match(names(public_dataset), dictionary$variable_name)
role_description <- standard_descriptions$description[match(dictionary$role[dictionary_row],
                                                            standard_descriptions$role)]
variable_summary <- tibble(variable_name = names(public_dataset)) %>%
  mutate(
    variable_description = coalesce(
      if_else(is_filled(dictionary$variable_description[dictionary_row]),
              dictionary$variable_description[dictionary_row], NA_character_),
      role_description,
      if_else(is_filled(dictionary$variable_label[dictionary_row]),
              dictionary$variable_label[dictionary_row], NA_character_),
      derived_variables$description[match(variable_name, derived_variables$variable_name)],
      if_else(str_starts(variable_name, fixed(source_column_prefix)),
              "Provenance of the record in the contributor's file.", NA_character_)),
    unit = coalesce(
      if_else(dictionary$kind[dictionary_row] %in% c("number", "whole_number") &
                is_filled(dictionary$unit_or_values[dictionary_row]),
              dictionary$unit_or_values[dictionary_row], NA_character_),
      standard_descriptions$unit[match(dictionary$role[dictionary_row], standard_descriptions$role)]),
    source = case_when(variable_name %in% dictionary$variable_name ~ "dictionary",
                       variable_name %in% derived_variables$variable_name ~ "derived",
                       TRUE ~ "source column"),
    values_in_public_file = map_int(variable_name, ~ sum(is_filled(public_dataset[[.x]]))),
    percent_complete = round(100 * values_in_public_file / max(nrow(public_dataset), 1), 1)
  )
undescribed <- variable_summary$variable_name[is.na(variable_summary$variable_description)]
if (length(undescribed) > 0) {
  warning("No description was found for: ", paste(undescribed, collapse = ", "),
          ". Add a variable_description column to the dictionary.", call. = FALSE)
}

# The variable summary is also saved as a Word table in the Scientific Data
# style.
variable_table_text <- variable_summary %>%
  transmute(Variable = variable_name,
            Description = coalesce(variable_description, "\u2014"),
            Unit = coalesce(unit, "\u2014"),
            Values = format(values_in_public_file, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE),
            `Complete (%)` = formatC(percent_complete, format = "f", digits = 1))
variable_table_footnote <- paste0(
  "Variables in the public file ", input_paths$public_file_name, ", in the order in which they appear. ",
  "Values: number of records with a value, of ", format(nrow(public_dataset), big.mark = ","),
  " records. Complete (%): percentage of records with a value. Units are given for numeric variables; ",
  "\u2014, not applicable. Coordinates use the WGS 84 datum. Empty values are written as NA.")
save_word_table(variable_table_text, variable_table_number, "Variables in the public BAM dataset.",
                variable_table_footnote, column_widths = c(1.8, 2.35, 0.6, 0.6, 0.9),
                right_aligned_columns = 4:5,
                path = file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "table_variable_summary.docx"))

# Every value changed by a correction rule, linked to its record_id.
corrections_applied <- bind_rows(tibble(step = character(), record_number = integer(),
                                        variable_name = character(), original_value = character(),
                                        corrected_value = character(), rule = character()),
                                 correction_log) %>%
  left_join(record_identifiers, by = "record_number") %>%
  mutate(in_public_file = if_else(record_number %in% public_record_numbers, "yes", "no")) %>%
  relocate(step, record_number, record_id)

# Manuscript figures are computed from the public file so that text and data
# agree.
type_counts <- table(factor(public_dataset[[tree_type_variable]], levels = c("baobab", "non-baobab")), useNA = "always")
public_dates <- na.omit(str_sub(public_dataset[[date_variable]], 1, 10))
public_dates <- public_dates[str_detect(public_dates, "^\\d{4}")]
manuscript_numbers <- tibble(
  quantity = c("Records in the public file", "Baobab records", "Non-baobab records", "Records of unrecorded type",
               "Unique baobab locations", "Countries", "Country list", "Source files",
               "Earliest observation date", "Latest observation date", "Records without a date",
               "Records naming their observer", "Different observers named", "Records with an anonymous observer",
               "Records removed: no valid position", "Records removed: imprecise position",
               "Records removed: outside mainland Africa", "Records removed: exact duplicates",
               "Records removed: repeated records",
               "Records removed: no stem measurement", "Records removed: implausible measurement"),
  value = c(nrow(public_dataset), type_counts[["baobab"]], type_counts[["non-baobab"]], sum(is.na(public_dataset[[tree_type_variable]])),
            nrow(distinct(filter(public_dataset, .data[[tree_type_variable]] %in% "baobab"), .data[[latitude_variable]], .data[[longitude_variable]])),
            n_distinct(na.omit(public_dataset$country)), paste(sort(unique(na.omit(public_dataset$country))), collapse = ", "),
            n_distinct(kept_records$source_file),  # Source columns are not in the public file.
            if (length(public_dates)) min(public_dates) else NA, if (length(public_dates)) max(public_dates) else NA,
            sum(!is_filled(public_dataset[[date_variable]])),
            if (!is.na(observer_name_variable)) sum(is_filled(public_dataset[[observer_name_variable]]) &
                                                    !public_dataset[[observer_name_variable]] %in% anonymous_label) else NA,
            if (!is.na(observer_name_variable)) n_distinct(setdiff(unlist(str_split(na.omit(public_dataset[[observer_name_variable]]), "; ")),
                                                                   anonymous_label)) else NA,
            if (!is.na(observer_name_variable)) sum(public_dataset[[observer_name_variable]] %in% anonymous_label) else NA,
            sum(removed_no_position), sum(removed_imprecise),
            sum(removed_outside), sum(duplicate_record),
            sum(repeated_record), sum(no_stem_measurement), sum(removed_implausible))
)
manuscript_numbers$value <- as.character(manuscript_numbers$value)

# Trees in the public file by data collection method and tree type.
collection_method_counts <- public_dataset %>%
  mutate(tree_type = coalesce(.data[[tree_type_variable]], "not recorded")) %>%
  count(data_collection_method, tree_type) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = tree_type, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
for (type in c("baobab", "non-baobab")) {
  if (!type %in% names(collection_method_counts)) collection_method_counts[[type]] <- 0L
}
collection_method_counts <- collection_method_counts %>%
  relocate(data_collection_method, baobab, `non-baobab`) %>%
  mutate(total = rowSums(across(-data_collection_method))) %>%
  arrange(desc(total))
manuscript_numbers <- bind_rows(manuscript_numbers, tibble(
  quantity = c(paste("Records from data collection method:", collection_method_counts$data_collection_method),
               paste("Baobab records from data collection method:", collection_method_counts$data_collection_method),
               paste("Non-baobab records from data collection method:", collection_method_counts$data_collection_method)),
  value = as.character(c(collection_method_counts$total, collection_method_counts$baobab,
                         collection_method_counts$`non-baobab`))))

records_by_file <- kept_records %>%
  count(source_file, tree_type = coalesce(.data[[tree_type_variable]], "not recorded")) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = tree_type, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  left_join(kept_records %>% group_by(source_file) %>%
              summarise(records = n(), countries = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(country))), collapse = ", "),
                        first_date = suppressWarnings(min(str_sub(.data[[date_variable]], 1, 10), na.rm = TRUE)),
                        last_date = suppressWarnings(max(str_sub(.data[[date_variable]], 1, 10), na.rm = TRUE)),
                        .groups = "drop"), by = "source_file") %>%
  arrange(desc(records))

# Flags, taxonomy and provenance are saved for internal review, linked by
# record_id.
record_flags_internal <- kept_records %>%
  select(record_id, any_of(c(tree_identity_variable, "qaqc_flags", "circumference_from_dbh",
                             "accepted_species_name", "taxonomic_status", "family", "wfo_taxon_id")),
         all_of(source_columns))

# write_excel_csv() keeps accented letters correct in Excel.
write_excel_csv(public_dataset, public_file_path, na = "NA")
write_excel_csv(qaqc_issues, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "qaqc_issues.csv"), na = "")
write_excel_csv(record_flags_internal, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "qaqc_record_flags.csv"), na = "")
write_excel_csv(manuscript_numbers, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "manuscript_numbers.csv"), na = "")
write_excel_csv(records_by_file, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "manuscript_table_records_by_file.csv"), na = "")
write_excel_csv(variable_summary, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "qaqc_variable_summary.csv"), na = "")
write_excel_csv(corrections_applied, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "qaqc_corrections_applied.csv"), na = "")
if (spelling_checked) {
  write_excel_csv(comment_spelling_review, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "comment_spelling_review.csv"),
                  na = "")
}
if (!is.na(observer_name_variable)) {
  write_excel_csv(observer_name_review, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "observer_name_review.csv"), na = "")
}
if (nrow(species_review) > 0) {
  write_excel_csv(species_review, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "species_name_review.csv"), na = "")
}
if (nrow(photo_lookup) > 0) {
  write_excel_csv(photo_lookup, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "photograph_name_lookup.csv"), na = "")
}
```

# Summary

```{r}
#| label: data-quality-numbers

# Records entering and leaving each validation stage. Each removed record is
# counted once, at the first stage it fails; flagged records are kept.
counts_file <- file.path(dirname(input_paths$harmonised_dataset_file), "harmonisation_counts.csv")
harmonisation_counts <- if (file.exists(counts_file)) read_as_text(counts_file) else NULL
count_of <- function(quantity) {
  if (is.null(harmonisation_counts)) return(NA_real_)
  as_number(harmonisation_counts$records[harmonisation_counts$quantity == quantity])[1]
}
records_read <- count_of("Tree records read from the contributor files")
if (!isTRUE(count_of("Records in the harmonised dataset") == number_of_records)) {
  warning("harmonisation_counts.csv does not match the harmonised dataset; run Harmonise_tree_data.R again.",
          call. = FALSE)
  records_read <- NA_real_
}

issue_records <- function(steps, severities) {
  issues <- current_issues()
  unique(na.omit(issues$record_number[issues$step %in% steps & issues$severity %in% severities]))
}
record_numbers <- seq_len(number_of_records)

after_compilation <- !empty_record
after_coordinates <- after_compilation & !removed_coordinates
after_boundary    <- after_coordinates & !removed_outside
after_measurement <- after_boundary & !removed_measurement
after_duplicates  <- keep_record
confirm(sum(after_duplicates) == nrow(public_dataset), "the data quality table does not match the public file.")

flagged_coordinates <- after_coordinates & record_numbers %in% issue_records("coordinates", "warning")
flagged_boundary    <- after_boundary & record_numbers %in% issue_records("study region", c("warning", "note"))
flagged_measurement <- after_measurement &
  record_numbers %in% issue_records(c("measurements", "multiple stems", "elephant damage"), "warning")
flagged_taxonomy    <- after_duplicates & is_filled(recorded_species) & !is_filled(working_data$accepted_species_name)

data_quality <- tibble(
  `Validation stage` = c("Initial data compilation", "Coordinate completeness and precision",
                         "Geographic boundary checks", "Measurement plausibility", "Duplicate screening",
                         "Taxonomic harmonisation", "Final public dataset"),
  `Records before` = c(records_read, sum(after_compilation), sum(after_coordinates), sum(after_boundary),
                       sum(after_measurement), sum(after_duplicates), nrow(public_dataset)),
  Removed = c(records_read - sum(after_compilation), sum(removed_coordinates), sum(removed_outside),
              sum(removed_measurement), sum(after_measurement & !after_duplicates), 0, NA),
  `Flagged (retained)` = c(NA, sum(flagged_coordinates), sum(flagged_boundary), sum(flagged_measurement), 0,
                           sum(flagged_taxonomy), NA),
  `Records after` = c(sum(after_compilation), sum(after_coordinates), sum(after_boundary),
                      sum(after_measurement), sum(after_duplicates), sum(after_duplicates), nrow(public_dataset))
)
data_quality_text <- data_quality %>%
  mutate(across(-`Validation stage`, ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), "\u2014", format(.x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))))

data_quality_footnote <- paste0(
  "Records after = records before \u2212 records removed. Each removed record is counted once, at the first ",
  "stage it fails. Flagged (retained): records kept in the dataset but marked for review. ",
  "Initial data compilation: tree records read from ", n_distinct(harmonised_data$source_file),
  " contributor files, less test submissions, dead trees, records of one tree merged across sheets, ",
  "identical records and records without values. Coordinate completeness and precision: records without a ",
  "valid coordinate pair, or recorded with fewer than ", minimum_recorded_decimal_places, " decimal places. ",
  "Geographic boundary checks: records more than ", coastal_tolerance_km, " km from mainland Africa were removed; ",
  "positions at sea within ", coastal_tolerance_km, " km of the coast were assigned the nearest country and flagged. ",
  "Measurement plausibility: stem, height or crown values beyond error limits, or no stem measurement, removed; ",
  "values above warning limits, stem-count conflicts and elephant damage reported where no wild elephants occur, ",
  "flagged. Duplicate screening: exact duplicates, repeated visits on one date, different trees at one position ",
  "in one file, and the same position, date and tree type in different files; the most complete record was kept. ",
  "Taxonomic harmonisation: records whose recorded species name had no exact species-level match in World Flora ",
  "Online, including sensitive species whose identity is withheld; no records are removed.")

# The table is saved as an editable Word document in the style of Scientific
# Data.
save_word_table(data_quality_text, 1, "Quantitative evidence of data quality and processing outcomes.",
                data_quality_footnote, column_widths = c(2.4, 0.95, 0.95, 0.95, 0.95),
                right_aligned_columns = 2:5,
                path = file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "table_data_quality.docx"))
write_excel_csv(data_quality, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "table_data_quality.csv"), na = "")
```

# Outputs and reproducibility

The following files were written to the results folder:

-   **table_data_quality.docx** (and .csv): records entering and leaving each validation stage (@tbl-data-quality), as an editable Word table.
-   **public_data/`r input_paths$public_file_name`**: the public dataset (`r format(nrow(public_dataset), big.mark = ",")` records, `r ncol(public_dataset)` columns).
-   **manuscript_numbers.csv** and **manuscript_table_records_by_file.csv**: every number and table quoted in the Data Descriptor, computed from the public file.
-   **qaqc_issues.csv**: every issue found, with the original value and the action taken (internal use only; it may contain personal data).
-   **qaqc_record_flags.csv**: for each public record (by `record_id`), the QA/QC flags, the WFO taxonomy (of which only `accepted_species_name` is published), whether the circumference was calculated from DBH, and the source columns (internal use only).
-   **qaqc_variable_summary.csv** and **table_variable_summary.docx**: the description, unit and completeness of each public variable (@tbl-completeness), the second as an editable Word table.
-   **qaqc_corrections_applied.csv**: every value changed by a correction rule (observer names, comments, rounding of elevation), with the original and corrected values, the rule applied and the `record_id` (internal use only).
-   **comment_spelling_review.csv**: words in comments not recognised by the spelling checker, with suggested corrections, for review (internal use only).
-   **observer_name_review.csv**: every person named, in alphabetical order, and the number of records (internal use only).
-   **species_name_review.csv**: species names without a species-level match, for correction (if any).
